column1: # boru corpus: core words (auto-generated from `boru describe` examples, verified interpret+check+compile)
def acc (flex [])  walk {mode: "depth"} {a:1 b:[2 3]} (m:Any => [acc (m.path) append])  acc
def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [mul x 2]]  3 (usurp f) apply
def inc fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]]  5 inc/v apply
def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  add {a:1 b:1} "B" r  find {a:1 b:1} r
def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  find {a:1 z:9} r
def r (patrun String)  add {a:1} "A" r  patterns r
import "boru:minilang"  def r ("AbcD" mini re '[a-z]+') end  r.fst.m
# The last full-stack sub-frontier row (the fifty-second increment,
# 2026-09-11): a full-stack word inside a WRAPPED CODE BODY. It compiled with
# an interpreter island while FoldFullStack was gated to the top unit; the
# fold is per-unit now, so the dispatch elides here exactly as it does at the
# top level. `depth` counts the body's own stack on both lanes, which is the
# fact the per-unit model rests on.

column3: a full-stack word inside a code body folds in that body's own unit
depth inside a body counts the BODY's stack — the element is in it

column1: # …and over EVENT-PRODUCED entries (the fifty-fourth increment): the half the
# per-unit fold had to leave islanded, because folding a PERMUTATION inside a
# body needs somewhere for the permuted residual to land and a body unit had
# no rebuild. reconcileResults takes the same seatResidualRebuild the program
# residual has now, so the fold is unrestricted per unit.

column3: a full-stack word over EVENT-produced entries folds in the body's own unit
…and the permuting roll with it, through the body unit's residual rebuild
a do body's permuted residual rebuilds exactly as the program's does
